Assignment Content

  1. Question 1

    Given the following database:

    person (driver_id, name, address, phone_number)

    car (license, model, year, insurance)

    accident (report_number, date, location, officer_name)

    owns (driver_id, license, date, payment)

    participated (driver_id, license, report_number, damage_amount)

    Identify the primary and foreign keys of table participated.

    The only way to identify a record in this table is to use a composite primary key consisting of all the foreign keys referencing the other tables in the ternary relationship, namely driver_ID, licence and report_number.
  2. Question 2

    Given the following database:

    person (driver_id, name, address, phone_number)

    car (license, model, year, insurance)

    accident (report_number, date, location, officer_name)

    owns (driver_id, license, date, payment)

    participated (driver_id, license, report_number, damage_amount)

    Identify the multi-valued attributes.

    All answers are incorrect as they are either the primary key of a table (and thus consist of a single value) or simply attributes that consist of a single value such as date or payment.
  3. Question 3

    Given the following database:

    person (driver_id, name, address, phone_number)

    car (license, model, year, insurance)

    accident (report_number, date, location, officer_name)

    owns (driver_id, license, date, payment)

    participated (driver_id, license, report_number, damage_amount)

    Identify the multi-valued attributes.

    The only correct answer is the one that includes phone number (home, mobile) and address (zip code, street, city). All the others cannot be correct since include attributes that consist of a single value such as driver_ID and report_number (primary keys).
  4. Question 4

    Given the following database:

    person (driver_id PK, name, address, phone_number)

    car (license PK, driver_id FK, model, year, insurance, date, payment)

    accident (report_number PK, date, location, officer_name, damage_amount)

    car_accident(license PK FK, report_number PK FK)

    Identify the cardinality of the relationship between person and car.

    Each person may own one or many cars, each car may be owned by one person. Therefore, the relationship has cardinality 1-to-many.
  5. Question 5

    Given the following database:

    person (driver_id PK, name, address, phone_number)

    car (license PK, driver_id FK, model, year, insurance, date, payment)

    accident (report_number PK, date, location, officer_name, damage_amount)

    car_accident(license PK FK, report_number PK FK)

    Identify the cardinality of the relationship between car and person.

    Each person may own one or many cars, each car may be owned by one person. Therefore, the relationship has cardinality 1-to-many.
  6. Question 6

    Which of the following statements is true?​

    The correct statement is that every entity in an E/R diagram has at least one key (in particular a primary key). The other statements are incorrect because: primary keys can be composite (thus may consist of more than one attribute), foreign keys can consist of a single attribute, each record must have different values in the attributes specified by a primary key.
  7. Question 7

    Consider the following entities, where the primary keys are underlined:​

    Student (FirstName, LastName, Age, YearOfStudy, EmailAddress, CourseOfStudy​)

    UniversityEmailAccount (EmailAddress, SecurityLevel, AccountCapacity​)

    What is the main issue with these entities in a real-world scenario?​

    The only correct statement is that the primary key of student may lead to issues as we expect to see students with the same pair of first and last names.

  15. Question 15

    Consider the following library management system database,

    authors (author_id, author_name)

    genres (genre_id, genre_name)

    publisher (publisher_id, publisher_name)

    books (book_id, book_title, publisher_id, publication_year, isbn)

    authors_books (author_id, book_id)

    genre_books (genre_id, book_id)

    members (member_id, member_name)

    transactions (transaction_id, book_id, member_id, checkout_date, return_date)

     In SQL, what type of key is the "author_id" column in the "authors" table?

    (Correct Answer: Primary Key – author_id in authors is a primary key as it uniquely identifies each record in table author)
  16. Question 16

    Consider the following library management system database,

    authors (author_id, author_name)

    genres (genre_id, genre_name)

    publisher (publisher_id, publisher_name)

    books (book_id, book_title, publisher_id, publication_year, isbn)

    authors_books (author_id, book_id)

    genre_books (genre_id, book_id)

    members (member_id, member_name)

    transactions (transaction_id, book_id, member_id, checkout_date, return_date)

    In SQL, what type of key is the "publisher_id" column in the "publisher" table?

    (Correct Answer: Primary Key – publisher_id in publisher table is a primary key as it uniquely identifies each record in table publisher)
  17. Question 17

    Consider the following library management system database,

    authors (author_id, author_name)

    genres (genre_id, genre_name)

    publisher (publisher_id, publisher_name)

    books (book_id, book_title, publisher_id, publication_year, isbn)

    authors_books (author_id, book_id)

    genre_books (genre_id, book_id)

    members (member_id, member_name)

    transactions (transaction_id, book_id, member_id, checkout_date, return_date)

    In SQL, what type of key is the "book_id" column in the "transactions" table?

    Correct Answer - Foreign Key - book_id in transactions table is a foreign key as it references to the book_id primary key of books table
  18. Question 18

    Consider the following library management system database,

    authors (author_id, author_name)

    genres (genre_id, genre_name)

    publisher (publisher_id, publisher_name)

    books (book_id, book_title, publisher_id, publication_year, isbn)

    authors_books (author_id, book_id)

    genre_books (genre_id, book_id)

    members (member_id, member_name)

    transactions (transaction_id, book_id, member_id, checkout_date, return_date)

    In SQL, what type of key is the "genre_id" and “book_id” columns in the "genre_books" table?

    Correct Answer - Composite Key - book_id and genre_id columns in genre_books table is a composite key as they uniquely identifies each record in table. These are also foreign keys.
  19. Question 19

    Consider the creation of two tables Department and Employee,

    CREATE TABLE Department (

       DepartmentID INT PRIMARY KEY,

       DepartmentName VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL

    )

    CREATE TABLE Employee (

       EmployeeID INT NOT NULL,

       FirstName VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,

       LastName VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,

       DateOfBirth DATE NOT NULL,

       DepartmentID NUMERIC NULL,

       CONSTRAINT PK_Employee PRIMARY KEY (EmployeeID),

       CONSTRAINT FK_Department_Employee FOREIGN KEY (DepartmentID)

           REFERENCES Department(DepartmentID)

    )

    Select the correct option.

    The query will give error because Department ID is foreign key in table Employee which has different datatype as in Department table. The datatype for foreign key DepartmentID in Employee table must match with Department Table.
